# Power management configuration options

# Copyright (c) 2018-2023, Intel Corporation.
# Copyright (c) 2023, Nordic Semiconductor ASA
# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0

menu "Power management"

config PM
	bool "Enable power management"
	help
	  Enable power management. This option enables the power management
	  subsystem.

if PM

config PM_DEVICE
	bool "Enable device power management"
	default y
	help
	  Enable device power management. This option enables the device
	  power management infrastructure. The SoC power management will be
	  kept active and it will be possible to suspend/resume devices.

config PM_DEVICE_RUNTIME
	bool "Enable device runtime power management"
	depends on PM_DEVICE
	help
	  Enable device runtime power management. This option enables the
	  device runtime power management infrastructure that allows devices
	  to be automatically suspended when not in use and resumed when
	  needed.

config PM_CPU_OPS_PSCI
	bool "Enable PSCI CPU power operations"
	depends on ARM64 && GIC_V2
	select ARM_PSCI
	help
	  Enable CPU power management operations using PSCI.

config PM_S2RAM
	bool "Enable System Suspend to RAM"
	depends on PM_DEVICE
	help
	  Enable system suspend to RAM support. This requires a platform that
	  is capable of saving and restoring its state.

config PM_POLICY_RESIDENCY
	bool "Residency policy"
	help
	  With this policy the system will try to enter the deepest possible
	  power state based on the ticks spent in idle.

config PM_POLICY_APP
	bool "Application-specific policy"
	help
	  With this policy the application can have some control over power
	  management. The application can decide which power states can be
	  used.

choice
	prompt "Power management policy"
	default PM_POLICY_RESIDENCY

config PM_POLICY_DUMMY
	bool "Dummy policy"
	help
	  This policy can be used by applications which do not require any
	  specific power management policy but want to be able to get/release
	  the CPU power constraints.

source "subsys/pm/policy/Kconfig"

endchoice

config PM_MIN_RESIDENCY_US
	int "Minimum residency for a power state to be used"
	default 0
	help
	  Some SoCs take a certain amount of time to enter and exit a
	  power state. If the time spent in idle is less than this, it is
	  not worth entering the state. This is SoC specific. The value
	  is in microseconds.

config PM_TICKLESS_IDLE
	bool "Enable tickless idle"
	depends on TICKLESS_IDLE
	default y
	help
	  Enable tickless idle in power management. This option is only
	  effective if the kernel supports tickless idle.

config PM_TICKLESS_IDLE_FALLBACK
	bool "Fallback to tickful idle if tickless is not effective"
	depends on PM_TICKLESS_IDLE
	help
	  Fallback to tickful idle if the duration of the idle period is
	  too short for tickless idle to be effective. This is useful
	  for systems that have a high overhead for entering and exiting
	  tickless idle.

config PM_LOG_LEVEL_OFF
	bool "No logging"
	depends on LOG
	help
	  Do not write any log messages.

config PM_LOG_LEVEL_ERR
	bool "Error"
	depends on LOG
	help
	  Write only error messages.

config PM_LOG_LEVEL_WRN
	bool "Warning"
	depends on LOG
	help
	  Write error and warning messages.

config PM_LOG_LEVEL_INF
	bool "Info"
	depends on LOG
	help
	  Write error, warning and info messages.

config PM_LOG_LEVEL_DBG
	bool "Debug"
	depends on LOG
	help
	  Write error, warning, info and debug messages.

config PM_LOG_LEVEL
	int
	default 0 if PM_LOG_LEVEL_OFF
	default 1 if PM_LOG_LEVEL_ERR
	default 2 if PM_LOG_LEVEL_WRN
	default 3 if PM_LOG_LEVEL_INF
	default 4 if PM_LOG_LEVEL_DBG
	depends on LOG

config PM_LOG
	bool
	default y if PM_LOG_LEVEL > 0
	depends on LOG

endif # PM

endmenu
